note: The rule table `perry-state --section next` evaluates (DESIGN-020 § 5.3, TASK-442). Overlays first, which always win; then `rules` in declared order. The first rule that fires is the primary; the next two that recommend a different command are the alternates. A predicate over a fact the payload cannot tell does not fire, and the fact is listed in `unknown[]`. Predicates compare typed values only — a fact path, an operator from `eq ne lt le gt ge in contains exists nonempty` (`in` asks whether a scalar fact is one of a declared list; `contains` asks whether a list fact holds a declared scalar), and a literal or a `{"threshold": name}` — combined with `all` / `any`. Each rule id is explained in `reference/next.md`. A command still reached through its direct entrance (`/perry goals init`, `plan-phase`, `plan-week`) moves to `/perry plan` when DESIGN-020 phase F ships that entrance.

phase_closable_ratio.note: Declared here because `schema/state-schema.json § thresholds` has no entry. The share of a phase's measured commit key results that must be met before closing it is recommended — the figure `goals/SKILL.md` has used for its KR-progress prompt.

asks_waiting_days.note: Declared here because `schema/state-schema.json § thresholds` has no entry. `/perry work nudge` surfaces questions idle this many days, so the rule recommends it at the same age.

weekly_late_weeks.note: Declared here because `schema/state-schema.json § thresholds` has no entry. A weekly report is late when the newest one is at least this many ISO weeks behind the current week — older than last week, as DESIGN-020 § 5.3 states it.

handoff_stale_days.note: Declared here because `schema/state-schema.json § thresholds` has no entry. DESIGN-020 § 5.3 rule 8.

phase_heartbeat_days.note: Declared here because `schema/state-schema.json § thresholds` has no entry. The default `goals/SKILL.md` used for its heartbeat prompt. A project's own `phase_heartbeat_days` setting is not in the payload, so it is not read.

architecture_review_days.note: Declared here because `schema/state-schema.json § thresholds` has no entry. The age at which `bin/perry-state` warns that `ARCHITECTURE.md` is overdue for review, so the recommendation arrives WITH the warning rather than at some second age. The warning does not read this file — it is raised before any rule is evaluated — so the number lives twice: here, and as `bin/perry-state § ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_DAYS`. Two tests guard the halves separately: `tests/test_next_section.py § TestTheRuleFile` reads both numbers and fails when they differ, and pins THIS rule's `ge`; `§ TestCadenceAndOperations` builds a project at exactly this age and fails unless the warning and the rule both speak on that one day, which is what catches a warning comparing `>` instead.
